findings.title: New modules miss future import, typed generics
findings.problem: code-quality.md Types And Imports requires `from __future__ import annotations` in new modules, parameterized generics instead of bare list/dict, and explicit return types on public functions. The new production module provisioning_clients_config.py has no future import (so load() at :73 needs a string forward reference) and _read_entries returns a bare `list` (:91). All 5 new test modules also omit the future import. There are bare annotations at test_provisioning_clients_config.py:42, test_provisioning_router.py:79 and test_provisioning_access.py:52, and the shared helper registered_clients (provisioning_clients_support.py:36) has no return type.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard for new code is unmet in one production module and five test modules. No automated gate enforces it, so the violation would merge unchecked.
findings.recommendation: Add `from __future__ import annotations` after the module docstring in provisioning_clients_config.py and in each new test module (provisioning_clients_support.py, test_provisioning_clients_config.py, test_provisioning_router.py, test_provisioning_access.py, test_provisioning_service.py). Annotate _read_entries as `-> list[object]` and drop the quotes around the load() return annotation. Parameterize the cited bare list/dict annotations, and give registered_clients its context-manager return type.
findings.check_notes: Future import added to provisioning_clients_config.py and all 5 test modules. _read_entries is -> list[object], load() is unquoted, cited bare generics are parameterized, registered_clients is typed.

fix.change: Future import added to provisioning_clients_config.py and the 5 new test modules; _read_entries -> list[object], unquoted load() return, cited bare generics parameterized, registered_clients typed AbstractContextManager[list[ProvisioningClient]]

findings.title: Client lookup does not canonicalize the user id
findings.problem: ProvisioningClient._normalize_user_id stores str(UUID(value)), the canonical hyphenated lowercase form, but find_client only applies user_id.lower() to the caller's id. That id is the IdP subject as received: AuthenticationService._validate_user_id_uuid (authentication_service.py:413-425) checks it with UUID() but does not canonicalize it. A subject in a non-canonical UUID form, such as 32 hex digits without hyphens, therefore never matches its registry entry.
findings.impact: When find_client returns None, enforce_provisioning_scope does nothing and is_service_account returns false. A registered client then escapes the 403 lock: the access control fails open, and the client is treated as a regular user who gets a personal project. Reachability is unconfirmed: it needs an IdP that emits non-canonical UUID subjects, and Keycloak emits canonical ones.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize both sides the same way. In find_client, parse the caller id with str(UUID(user_id)) and return None on ValueError. Add a test that finds a registered id when it is given hyphen-less or in uppercase.
findings.check_notes: find_client canonicalizes via str(UUID(user_id)) and returns None on ValueError. All 4 registry lookups route through it. Hyphen-less, uppercase and non-UUID tests were added.

fix.change: find_client canonicalizes the caller id with str(UUID(...)) and returns None for a non-UUID id

findings.title: Spec-mandated email normalization breaks security standard
findings.problem: NormalizedEmail (models/provisioning.py:22-26) runs strip().lower() in a BeforeValidator before EmailStr parses the client-supplied member_email of GET /v1/provisioning/projects (routers/provisioning/projects.py:53). security-patterns.md Untrusted Input Handling lists stripping and silent coercion before parsing under Avoid. Spec Design 5 explicitly requires the input to be normalized and the removed ServiceNow route's behaviour to be kept.
findings.impact: The third-party-facing lookup decides whose project memberships to disclose from a repaired value rather than the value sent: padded input returns 200 instead of 422. The approved spec and a documented security standard disagree, so the fix needs a human decision.
findings.recommendation: Decide one: (a) drop the BeforeValidator so EmailStr rejects padded input with 422, leave case folding to user_repository.get_by_emails, and update spec Design 5 and the OpenAPI parameter description; or (b) keep the normalization and record email case/whitespace folding as an accepted exception in .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md.
findings.check_notes: Mapped decision chose option (a), with a rationale. The BeforeValidator was dropped, so the route takes list[EmailStr]. EmailStr's own trimming is accepted.

fix.change: member_email is list[EmailStr] with no pre-parse normalization; NormalizedEmail/_strip_and_lowercase moved back to models/servicenow_integration.py for the unrouted budget model; OpenAPI description, baseline and spec Design 5 updated

decision.outcome: Option (a): drop the BeforeValidator normalization from the member_email query parameter
decision.rationale: User chose to follow security-patterns.md Untrusted Input Handling over spec Design 5; the lookup now takes list[EmailStr], case folding is left to user_repository.get_by_emails, spec Design 5 and the OpenAPI parameter description were updated. Note: pydantic 2.13.5 EmailStr itself trims surrounding whitespace, so padded input still parses (200), not 422. User confirmed keeping this: EmailStr's own trimming is accepted and no rejecting validator is added.

findings.title: Retained budget model lost its validator tests
findings.problem: Deleting tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_servicenow_integration_router.py also removed TestServiceNowBudgetRequest. Those tests covered: set requires platform > 0; cancel clears amounts and admin_emails; non-finite and negative amounts are rejected; names are lowercased and defaulted; field limits hold. ServiceNowBudgetRequest stays, and this diff edits its _normalize_names (:75) to call the moved strip_and_lowercase. The remaining service tests use the model only as valid input, and no test now asserts its validation rules.
findings.impact: Spec Design 7 keeps the budget logic and what it uses in place, unrouted, for EPMCDME-16905, on the premise that the logic is 'implemented and tested'. Its input-validation rules, including the line this change edited, are no longer covered by any test, so 16905 would expose them to clients untested.
findings.recommendation: Restore the TestServiceNowBudgetRequest cases in a test module next to the model, for example tests/codemie/rest_api/models/test_servicenow_integration.py. Leave out the NormalizedEmail query-parameter case, which now belongs to the provisioning models.
findings.check_notes: TestServiceNowBudgetRequest is restored in tests/codemie/rest_api/models/test_servicenow_integration.py. It covers set platform>0, cancel clearing, negative/inf/nan, name lowercasing and defaults, and field limits.
